sources.title: A1 – Kornkjeden i Norge
sources.citationText: Food Systems 2026 (internal synthesis). A1 – Kornkjeden i Norge. Published 2026-09-08. Consulted 2026-09-15.
sources.note: Read through the GitHub connector. Reused as the existing research baseline and a bounded gap report, NOT independent primary proof of world-level absence. No historical file was changed.

evidence.locator: Opening share paragraph; scope paragraph beginning "I kartlegginga".
evidence.note: Rounded reported shares total 99.9%. Reconstruct HHI without renormalising; not an official unrounded HHI observation.
Target and approximate normal grain-use equivalence; neither actual September 2026 stock nor three months of complete diets.

evidence.locator: Opening award paragraph and "Tidligere inngått kontrakter om 60 000 tonn".
evidence.note: Contract cohorts are separate from dated physical inventory; do not add them to an observed stock.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning "De fire aktørene"; sentence beginning "Ved utgangen av 2024".
evidence.note: A historical agency-reported stock, not a current estimate and not claimed to be the latest report.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 66 as cited by existing A1-S001; primary passage unavailable in this run.
evidence.note: Inherited candidate from A1, not independently verified here. No interpolation to September 2026.

evidence.locator: Sections "Staten kjøper lagringstjenester" and "Slik skal statens beredskapslagring organiseres".
evidence.note: State owns the grain; commercial operators provide storage and rotation; ministry and directorate roles are described at programme level.

evidence.locator: "Dekning av spørsmålene", gaps A1-G001 and A1-G002, and sections 2–3.
evidence.note: The existing study reports missing comparable disruption throughput, current node inventory and operating evidence within its searched material. This is not proof no such data exists.

claims.text: This historical comparison covers traditional Norwegian grocery retail with physical sales from stores; it excludes online retail from the authority’s reported scope.
claims.limits: Not all food purchases, Nordic retail, local catchment competition, or a current-2026 market measure.

claims.text: Using the published rounded 2024 revenue shares, the reconstructed HHI is {{hhi}} and CR3 is {{cr3}}%. HHI is an index; CR3 is a percentage.
claims.limits: Sum squared percentage shares, round HHI to an integer, and sum the three largest shares for CR3. Inputs sum to 99.9% through rounding; no renormalisation. Compare with existing CA-004, without changing its review status.

claims.text: These measures describe the distribution of turnover. They do not identify the cause of prices, prove unlawful conduct, or measure resilience. Those would require separate evidence and definitions.
claims.limits: Analytical boundary, not a causal finding or legal assessment.

claims.text: The programme target is {{grain-target.tonnes}} tonnes of food wheat by 2029. The agency relates this to about {{grain-target.normalMonths}} months of normal grain use by bakeries, industry and households.
claims.limits: A future target, not measured current stock, delivered meals, or a guarantee of complete nutrition.

claims.text: Awarded storage cohorts are {{grain-contracts.start2024and2025}} tonnes starting in 2024/2025, {{grain-contracts.start2026and2027}} in 2026/2027, and {{grain-contracts.start2028and2029}} in 2028/2029.
claims.limits: Contracted quantities and start years; not measurements of filled silos on those dates.

claims.text: The agency reported {{grain-stock-2024.tonnes}} tonnes on reserve at the end of 2024. This remains a dated historical observation, not the latest inventory claim.
claims.limits: Do not extrapolate yearly purchases into a September 2026 inventory.

claims.text: The inherited A1 candidate records {{grain-stock-2025.tonnes}} tonnes at the end of 2025.
claims.limits: BLOCKED pending independent reading of the primary passage. Source access failure is not evidence that the reported quantity is false. This does not retract or overwrite A1.

claims.text: The state owns the wheat, while grain traders or food-flour mills provide storage. Operators maintain quality through rotation with their commercial grain. The ministry has overall responsibility and the directorate administers the arrangement.
claims.limits: Programme-level organisation as described in 2024. This source does not establish emergency release timings or actual continuity of each operator.

claims.text: Stored grain becomes useful food only through connected functions: release and allocation; quality selection and handling; milling; packaging or bulk delivery; baking or other preparation; distribution; and access by recipients. This is the pilot’s working chain, not a claim that a particular route has been observed functioning under disruption.
claims.limits: A conceptual explanation. No facility-specific resilience, weakest-node ranking or delivery duration is inferred.

claims.text: Tonnes in storage, tonnes of raw grain processed per hour, tonnes of flour produced, and meals delivered are different measurements. A defensible delivery calculation needs compatible units, conversion yields, start-up delays, recipient needs and disruption-specific operating capacities. Missing inputs remain unknown.
claims.limits: Dimensional and logical reasoning, not an empirical estimate. Nominal annual capacity cannot be substituted for spare emergency throughput.

claims.text: The existing A1 study found partial node and route information but did not establish a complete, comparable disruption-capacity chain in its checked sources. Its identified inventory and throughput gaps remain research questions in this pilot.
claims.limits: Statement about the repository study, not a claim that no relevant public or private measurements exist.

claims.text: Competence belongs inside the chain: grain-quality judgement, milling and maintenance, changes to recipes or preparation, transport coordination, and allocation decisions. The research task is to test which capabilities limit performance in a specified event, and whether documented substitutes exist—not infer capability from headcounts alone.
claims.limits: Candidate mechanism and research framing. The pilot does not establish staffing levels, skill shortages or causal effects.

claims.text: The reserve addresses one form of exposure: grain availability. If downstream conversion and delivery remain functional, stock can address a raw-material interruption. If those functions cannot operate, a larger nominal stock alone does not establish more delivered meals. The relevant test is performance under a stated disruption, not the stock headline alone.
claims.limits: Conditional reasoning, not a prediction of failure. Additional imports, alternative facilities, substitutions and recovery could alter the outcome.

gaps.question: What is the equivalent measure for 2026?
gaps.missing: This pilot deliberately uses 2024, not a current market series.
gaps.nextEvidence: A compatible authority series for the requested year and market boundary.
gaps.searchBoundary: Only the 2024 authority HTML and existing CA-004 context were used.

gaps.question: How much usable reserve grain is held on 15 September 2026?
gaps.missing: A dated, reconciled inventory for that date; quality and ownership scope are not supplied by the contract totals.
gaps.nextEvidence: A dated agency/operator inventory with commodity, unit, quality, operator and reconciliation to the national scope.
gaps.searchBoundary: A1 as of 8 September and the five named official source leads checked in this pilot; no operator contacted.

gaps.question: Can the end-2025 stock be independently rechecked?
gaps.missing: The annual-report PDF exceeded this run’s fetch limits; printed page 66 was not reread.
gaps.nextEvidence: Acquire the official PDF through the controlled source workflow; inspect page 66, verify document identity and bind the exact passage.
gaps.searchBoundary: Official report landing page plus both linked government PDF locations attempted on 15 September; this is an access limit, not a world-level data gap.

gaps.question: What can the connected chain deliver under one defined disruption?
gaps.missing: Compatible node and route throughput, spare capacity, yields, start-up delays and dependencies for the same scenario.
gaps.nextEvidence: An operator-checked chain with raw/product units, dates, energy, packaging, transport, downtime and rerouting assumptions.
gaps.searchBoundary: A1-G002 and this bounded source set; no operational test or confidential capacity dataset inspected.

gaps.question: How quickly can reserves be released and allocated?
gaps.missing: A current executable release process, decision authority, trigger and observed lead time.
gaps.nextEvidence: Current controlled procedure plus a dated exercise or event record of decisions and release timing.
gaps.searchBoundary: 2024 programme description and A1; no current emergency procedure was independently opened.

gaps.question: Which skills are limiting and substitutable?
gaps.missing: Task-level competence, availability, replacement time and evidence of adaptation during disruption.
gaps.nextEvidence: Consented interviews or exercise/incident evidence linked to specific tasks and conditions; test alternative explanations.
gaps.searchBoundary: A1 and the conceptual chain only; no workforce survey, interviews or skills assessment conducted here.

gaps.question: How many people can receive adequate meals, and for how long?
gaps.missing: Population, dietary requirement, usable product allocation, preparation capacity and delivery evidence.
gaps.nextEvidence: Define recipients and nutrition scope, then connect dated stock, conversion and delivery observations; retain unknown cells.
gaps.searchBoundary: No population denominator or full-chain scenario inputs have been established in this pilot.

topics.title: From grain reserves to meals: a first Norwegian explanation
topics.scope: Food wheat in Norway, from storage through conversion and distribution to recipients. Evidence checked on 15 September 2026. A bounded candidate synthesis building on A1, not a full systematic review, operational forecast or national readiness assessment.
